title: What If Every Whale Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every whale vanished? It could change the air you breathe.
Whale waste carries iron and nitrogen, the food of phytoplankton. Whales dive deep, feed, then release it near the surface.
Phytoplankton make at least half of the oxygen in the air, and absorb about thirty-seven billion tons of carbon dioxide a year.
Researchers estimate even one percent more phytoplankton would capture hundreds of millions of extra tons of carbon dioxide a year. Losing whales pushes the other way.
And each great whale locks away about thirty-three tons of carbon dioxide. When it dies and sinks, that stays down for centuries.
Whales are already under a quarter of their numbers before whaling. Vanishing would erase a living climate machine.
